parcels.name: Root title · the whole farm before 1877
parcels.desc: Great House (Cydfin / Tŷ Mawr): the farmhouse with Parcels A and B together, before the 1877 split. NLW Bute D219 lists “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm (107 a.)”, leases 1552–1824.

parcels.name: Lordship of the manor of Llandough
parcels.desc: The manorial lordship (rents, courts, waste), which passed separately from the farm freehold until both reached the Bute Estate.

parcels.name: Parcel A
parcels.desc: The house parcel, whole: farmhouse, yard, woodland and green, about 10 acres (the 1877 split).

parcels.name: Parcel A1 · north wood
parcels.desc: Top third of Parcel A: the woodland (OS 1900 field 45). Later title WA735527.

parcels.name: Parcel A2 · house & yard
parcels.desc: Middle third: farmhouse, yard and buildings (OS 1900 field 70). Title WA240304 (1983), merged into WA231076 (1987).

parcels.name: Parcel A3 · the green
parcels.desc: Lower third: the green by Leckwith Road, village green VG41 (1970).

parcels.name: Parcel B · the fields
parcels.desc: The fields east of the house, about 9 acres (OS 1900 fields 71 and 78; 1939 tenancy plan). Title WA231076.

parcels.name: Woods round the farm
parcels.desc: Woods and land near the farm in the same estates. A link to Parcel A is not established.

transfers.label: 1547 lease
transfers.instrument: A 1,000-year lease of Cydwin (the Great House) from Sir George Herbert to Vaughan. The lease itself is not in hand.
transfers.note: Sir George Herbert held the manor of Llandough by 1545 (rent-roll in Cardiff Records). The Vaughans, a minor gentry family, held the Great House, the chief freehold farm of the parish, from the mid-16th century to the later 18th (Heneb HER). Historical family only. A present-day family of the same name has told us it is not related.

transfers.label: 1767 marriage
transfers.instrument: Inheritance by marriage: William Hurst and Calvert Richard Jones had married two heiresses of this branch of the Herbert family, and by 1767 held the manors of Dinas Powys, Llandough East and Cogan.
transfers.note: Cardiff Records: from 1545 the manor passed from Sir George Herbert to his grandson Sir William Herbert, and stayed with the Herberts of Cogan Pill for several generations.

root.name: Root title chain
root.intro: The documentary root: the Herbert manor, the Vaughans’ Great House, the Bute Estate, then the 1877 split into Parcel A and Parcel B. Solid = a dated record on file; dashed = gap, source to add.

steps.label: Herbert → Vaughan: the Great House (Cydwin)
steps.text: Sir George Herbert, lord of the manor of Llandough by 1545, grants the Vaughans a 1,000-year lease of Cydwin, the Great House (research note GHF-E178; Evidence Register EV-0002, lease not yet in hand). The Heneb HER records the Vaughans holding the Great House, the chief freehold farm of the parish, from the mid-16th century to the later 18th. Historical families only.

src.t: GHF-E178 · 1547 Herbert lease of Cydwin to Vaughan (research note)
Heneb HER GGAT02038s · Great House Farm (Vaughan freehold; Bute in the early 19th century)
Cardiff Records vol. 2, “The manors of Cardiff district” (Cogan; Llandough)
History of Parliament: HERBERT, George (1494/95–1570), of Swansea

steps.label: Vaughan → Bute Estate: freehold of the Great House
steps.text: The Heneb HER records the Bute Estate holding the Great House freehold in the early 19th century, with the manorial courts for Llandough and Leckwith held in the house. The conveyance, its date and who sold are not located: gap, source to add. The Bute records for “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm” run 1552–1824 (EV-0003). The lordship of the manor reached Bute separately: Herbert → Hurst & Jones by 1767 → Bute 1793.

src.t: Heneb HER GGAT02038s · Great House Farm (Vaughan freehold; Bute in the early 19th century)
EV-0003 · Bute Estate records 1552–1824 naming Cydfin / Ty Mawr Farm (Evidence Register)

steps.label: 1877 split · Parcel A to Daniel Thomas & Son
steps.text: The Bute Estate parts with the farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres (Parcel A) to Daniel Thomas & Son of the Llandough lime works, by sale or quarry lease, and keeps about 9 acres (Parcel B). Known from Mary (Nancy) Williams’s statement (Timeline page 33); the 1877 agreement (EV-0006) is not yet located. The NLW Bute catalogue has Llandough land “formerly part of Great House Farm” for the lime works, 1876–1912 (EV-0291).

src.t: EV-0291 · NLW Bute Estate catalogue D153 (Llandough limeworks land, 1876–1912)
Legal Wiki · Three parts of Parcel A (page 3356)

steps.label: 1877 split · Parcel B kept by the Bute Estate, then Mountjoy Ltd (1926)
steps.text: In 1877 the Bute Estate keeps about 9 acres “up on the top” (Parcel B; Timeline page 33). Bute still lets it in 1916 (yearly tenancy with plan, EV-0014). In 1926 the remaining Bute property is incorporated as Mountjoy Ltd (Glamorgan Archives DA catalogue). The records place Mountjoy in 1926, not 1877.

src.t: EV-0014 · 1916 Bute yearly tenancy, with plan
Glamorgan Archives DA catalogue (Bute estate history)

steps.label: Parcel B · Mountjoy / Bute → Western Ground Rents
steps.text: Conveyance on sale, Mountjoy / Bute to Western Ground Rents Ltd, 25 Dec 1938 (recited in later WGR deeds). The deed and its plan are not held, so exactly which land it carried is still open. A 1939 tenancy plan shows WGR letting Parcel B only.

steps.label: Parcel B · Western Ground Rents → BP Pension Trust
steps.text: Conveyance, WGR to BP Pension Trust, recited as the root of BP’s title. For the house it carried the benefit of the 1962 order. BP’s agreed bid of 15 Feb 1969 took WGR’s properties “for their pension fund” (press). In September 1974 BP applied for leave to enforce the 1962 order. The conveyance and plan are not held.

src.t: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (judgment)
EV-0043 · 1969 conveyance, WGR to BP Pension Trust
EV-0288 · 1968–69 press on the WGR takeover

steps.title: WA231076
steps.label: Parcel B · BP Properties registers WA231076
steps.text: BP Properties Ltd applies to register title WA231076 (the farm). The application date is in HM Land Registry’s file schedule. The transfer from BP Pension Trust to BP Properties is not held.

steps.label: Parcel A · the family holds it after the last rent to Thomas
steps.text: Quarrying ends and the last rent of about £4 is paid to Alfred Thomas, son of Daniel Thomas; on the family’s case the 1877 arrangement then takes effect and Parcel A passes to the Williams family (Mary’s statement; the 1928 receipt, EV-0016, is pending). No deed is held.

steps.label: Parcel A · no conveyance from Daniel Thomas & Son or the family on record
steps.text: No deed on file carries Parcel A, or the house and yard A(2), from Daniel Thomas & Son, or from the family who held it from 1928, to Western Ground Rents, BP or anyone else. The house title WA240304 was first registered in 1983 out of the 💩 chain instead, which starts at the 💩 on the ring (1955 order → 1962 → … → 1983). Gap: source to add, if such a deed exists.
